title: N-nitrosodimethylamine-Contaminated Valsartan and Risk of Cancer: A Nationwide Study of 1.4 Million Valsartan Users
authors: Mansouri I, Botton J, Semenzato L, Haddy N, Zureik M
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
followUp: median 4.0 years exposed (4,253,623 person-years) and 3.5 years unexposed (2,565,339 person-years)
population: About 1.4 million French residents aged 40 to 80 years without previous cancer who used valsartan between 2013 and 2017, in the Système National des Données de Santé; authors at EPI-PHARE, a joint unit of the French medicines agency (ANSM) and national health insurance
funder: Sources of Funding: None. Disclosures: None.
result: 986,126 patients exposed to NDMA-contaminated and 670,388 to uncontaminated valsartan. Overall cancer: adjusted hazard ratio 0.99 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.0). Liver cancer 1.12 (1.04 to 1.22) and melanoma 1.10 (1.03 to 1.18), estimated at a mean of 3.7 and 5.8 extra cases per 100,000 person-years respectively.
